units.zh: 世家四○南漢劉氏
units.en: Hereditary Houses 4: The Southern Han Liu.
units.literal: Hereditary Houses 4 — The Liu Clan of Southern Han.

units.zh: 南漢劉鋹，其先蔡州上蔡人，高祖安仁，仕唐為潮州刺史，因家嶺表。
units.en: Liu Chang of Southern Han came from a line originally of Shangcai in Cai Prefecture. His great-grandfather Anren had served the Tang as prefect of Chaozhou and settled his family in Lingnan.
units.literal: Liu Chang of Southern Han — his ancestors were men of Shangcai in Cai Prefecture; his great-grandfather Anren served the Tang as prefect of Chaozhou and thereupon made his home in Lingnan.

units.zh: 安仁生謙，為廣州牙校，累遷封州刺史、賀水鎮遏使。
units.en: Anren's son Qian served as a military aide at Guangzhou and rose through successive appointments to prefect of Feng and commissioner at Hesui.
units.literal: Anren begat Qian, who served as a military aide at Guangzhou and was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Feng Prefecture and military commissioner of Hesui.

units.zh: 謙生隱，謙卒，隱代領其任。
units.en: Qian's son Yin succeeded him when Qian died and assumed his command.
units.literal: Qian begat Yin; when Qian died, Yin took over his post in his stead.

units.zh: 唐昭宗以薛王知柔鎮南海，辟為行軍司馬，委以兵柄。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong posted the Prince of Xue, Zhi Rou, to the South Seas, Yin was made his chief of staff on campaign and given control of the army.
units.literal: Emperor Zhaozong of Tang sent the Prince of Xue, Zhi Rou, to govern the South Seas and appointed Yin chief of staff on campaign, entrusting him with military authority.

units.zh: 及宰相徐彥若代知柔，以為節度副使。
units.en: When Chief Minister Xu Yanruo succeeded Zhi Rou, Yin was appointed deputy military commissioner.
units.literal: When the chief minister Xu Yanruo replaced Zhi Rou, Yin was made deputy military commissioner.

units.zh: 時唐室已季，彥若威令不振，事皆決於隱。
units.en: The Tang dynasty was already in decline, and Yanruo's authority no longer commanded obedience; Yin decided everything.
units.literal: The Tang house was already in its last days; Yanruo's prestige and orders did not carry weight, and all affairs were decided by Yin.

units.zh: 彥若卒，遺表薦隱自代，昭宗不從，以崔遠代之。
units.en: On Yanruo's death he recommended Yin to succeed him in a final memorial, but Zhaozong refused and appointed Cui Yuan instead.
units.literal: When Yanruo died he left a memorial recommending Yin to succeed him; Zhaozong did not assent and sent Cui Yuan in his place.

units.zh: 遠至江陵，遷延不進，乃以隱為留後，未幾，授以節旄。
units.en: Cui Yuan reached Jiangling but lingered without advancing, so Yin was made acting commissioner; shortly afterward he received the full commission.
units.literal: Yuan reached Jiangling but delayed and did not advance; Yin was then made acting commissioner, and before long he was granted the commissioner's insignia.

units.zh: 梁開平初，兼靜海軍節度使，封南海王。
units.en: Early in the Liang Kaiping period he was also made military commissioner of the Jinghai army and created Prince of the Southern Sea.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Liang dynasty's Kaiping era he additionally held the commission of the Jinghai army and was enfeoffed as Prince of the Southern Sea.

units.zh: 隱卒，弟陟襲位。
units.en: After Yin died, his younger brother Zhi took the throne.
units.literal: When Yin died, his younger brother Zhi succeeded to the position.

units.zh: 貞明三年，僭帝號，國稱大漢，改元乾亨，行郊祀禮。
units.en: In the third year of Zhenming he took an imperial title, named his state Great Han, adopted the era Qianheng, and performed suburban sacrifices.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he arrogated an imperial title; the state was called Great Han, the era name was Qianheng, and suburban sacrifices were performed.

units.zh: 改名岩，又改龔，終改龑。
units.en: He changed his name first to Yan, then to Gong, and at last to a character of his own devising.
units.literal: He changed his name to Yan, then to Gong, and finally to a character of his own invention.

units.zh: 「龑」讀為「儼」，字書不載，蓋其妄作也。
units.en: The character 龑 was pronounced "yan," like the ordinary graph for that sound; it appears in no dictionary and was plainly his own fabrication.
units.literal: The character 龑 is read as "yan," homophonous with the standard character for that sound; it does not appear in dictionaries — evidently he invented it himself.

units.zh: 晉天福七年，卒，子玢嗣，為弟晟所殺。
units.en: He died in the seventh year of Later Jin's Tianfu. His son Bin succeeded him but was killed by his younger brother Sheng.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Later Jin's Tianfu he died; his son Bin succeeded but was killed by his younger brother Sheng.

units.zh: 晟遂自立，性尤酷暴，周顯德五年，卒，事具《五代史》。
units.en: Sheng then seized power himself. He was exceptionally cruel and violent, and died in the fifth year of Later Zhou's Xiande; the full story is given in the History of the Five Dynasties.
units.literal: Sheng then established himself in power; his nature was especially cruel and violent. In the fifth year of Later Zhou's Xiande he died; the full account is in the History of the Five Dynasties.

units.zh: 鋹即晟長子也，初名繼興，封衛王，襲父位，改今名，改元大寶。
units.en: Chang was Sheng's eldest son, originally named Jixing and enfeoffed Prince of Wei. On succeeding his father he took his present name and proclaimed the era Dabao.
units.literal: Chang was Sheng's eldest son; he was first named Jixing, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and on succeeding his father changed to his present name and era to Dabao.

units.zh: 性昏懦，委政宦官龔澄樞及才人盧瓊仙，每詳覽可否，皆瓊仙指之。
units.en: He was dull and timid by nature and left government to the eunuch Gong Chengshu and the talented concubine Lu Qiongxian; whenever he weighed what might be done, Qiongxian's finger decided it.
units.literal: His character was dull and timid; he entrusted government to the eunuch Gong Chengshu and the talented concubine Lu Qiongxian; whenever he scrutinized what was permissible, it was Qiongxian who pointed it out.

units.zh: 鋹日與宮人、波斯女等遊戲。
units.en: Chang passed his days in games with palace women, Persian women, and the like.
units.literal: Chang spent his days at play with palace women, Persian women, and the like.

units.zh: 內官陳延壽引女巫樊胡入宮，言玉皇遣樊胡命鋹為太子皇帝，乃於宮中施帷幄，羅列珍玩，設玉皇坐。
units.en: The inner attendant Chen Yanshou introduced the witch Fan Hu, who claimed the Jade Emperor had sent her to name Chang Crown Prince Emperor. Within the palace they hung silken curtains, displayed rare treasures, and set out a throne for the Jade Emperor.
units.literal: The inner attendant Chen Yanshou brought the shamaness Fan Hu into the palace, saying the Jade Emperor had sent Fan Hu to appoint Chang as Crown Prince Emperor; in the palace silken curtains were hung, rare treasures arrayed, and a seat for the Jade Emperor set up.

units.zh: 樊胡遠遊冠、紫衣、紫霞裙，坐宣禍福，令鋹再拜聽命；
units.en: Fan Hu wore a traveling cap, purple robes, and a purple cloud skirt, sat proclaiming fortune and disaster, and made Chang bow twice to receive her commands;
units.literal: Fan Hu wore a distant-traveling cap, purple robes, and a purple cloud skirt, sat announcing fortune and calamity, and ordered Chang to bow twice and heed commands;

units.zh: 嘗雲瓊仙、澄樞、延壽皆玉皇遣輔太子皇帝，有過不得治。
units.en: She once declared that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Yanshou had all been sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the Crown Prince Emperor and that he must not punish them even if they erred.
units.literal: She once declared that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Yanshou were all sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the Crown Prince Emperor, and that if they erred he must not punish them.

units.zh: 又有梁山師、馬媼、何擬之徒出入宮掖。
units.en: Others such as Liang Shanshi, Old Woman Ma, and He Ni also moved freely through the inner palace.
units.literal: Others such as Liang Shanshi, Old Woman Ma, and He Ni also came and went within the inner palace.

units.zh: 宮中婦人皆具冠帶，領外事。
units.en: Every woman in the palace wore official cap and sash and took charge of outside affairs.
units.literal: All women in the palace wore caps and sashes and managed external affairs.

units.zh: 初，龑雖寵任中官，其數裁三百餘，位不過掖庭諸局令丞。
units.en: At first, even though that ruler favored eunuchs, their number was barely three hundred, and none rose above the chiefs and assistants of the palace bureaus.
units.literal: At first, though the emperor with the invented name favored eunuchs, their number was limited to just over three hundred, and ranks did not exceed bureau chiefs and assistant commissioners of the palace domestic offices.

units.zh: 至晟時千餘人，稍增內常侍、諸謁者之稱。
units.en: Under Sheng they numbered more than a thousand, and titles such as inner regular attendant and various commissioners were gradually introduced.
units.literal: By Sheng's time there were over a thousand, and titles of inner regular attendant and various commissioners were gradually added.

units.zh: 至鋹漸至七千餘，有為三師、三公，但其上加「內」字，諸使名不翅二百，女官亦有師傅、令仆之號。
units.en: Under Chang they eventually exceeded seven thousand. Some held the ranks of the Three Preceptors and Three Excellencies with only the prefix "inner" added; commissioner titles alone numbered no fewer than two hundred, and female officials too bore titles of tutor, steward, and chief steward.
units.literal: Under Chang they gradually reached more than seven thousand; some held the ranks of the Three Preceptors and Three Excellencies, with only the prefix "inner" added; commissioner titles numbered no fewer than two hundred; female officials also had titles of tutor, steward, and chief steward.

units.zh: 目百官為「門外人」，群臣小過及士人、釋、道有才略可備問者，皆下蠶室，令得出入宮闈。
units.en: He called the civil officials "people outside the gate." Officials guilty of minor faults, and any scholar, Buddhist, or Daoist with talent worth consulting, were castrated and made to enter and leave the inner palace at will.
units.literal: He regarded the hundred officials as "people outside the gate"; officials guilty of minor faults, and scholars, Buddhists, and Daoists with talent useful for consultation, were all sent to the silkworm chamber so they could come and go within the palace.

units.zh: 作燒煮剝剔、刀山劍樹之刑，或令罪人鬥虎抵象。
units.en: He invented punishments of boiling alive, flaying, dismemberment, and mountains of blades and forests of swords, or set criminals to fight tigers and elephants.
units.literal: He devised punishments of boiling, flaying, cutting apart, mountains of knives and forests of swords, or made culprits fight tigers or elephants.

units.zh: 又賦斂煩重，邕民入城者人輸一錢，瓊州米斗稅四五錢。
units.en: His levies were oppressive as well: every person entering the capital at Yong paid one cash, and a peck of rice at Qiong Prefecture carried a tax of four or five cash.
units.literal: Levies were also heavy and vexatious; people entering the city of Yong paid one cash per person; a peck of rice at Qiong Prefecture was taxed four or five cash.

units.zh: 置媚川都，定其課，令入海五百尺采珠。
units.en: He set up the Meichuan Command, fixed its levy, and ordered divers five hundred feet into the sea to collect pearls.
units.literal: He established the Meichuan Command and fixed its quota, ordering men to dive five hundred feet into the sea to gather pearls.

units.zh: 所居宮殿以珠、玳瑁飾之。
units.en: The palaces where he lived were decorated with pearls and tortoise shell.
units.literal: The palaces he dwelt in were adorned with pearls and tortoise shell.

units.zh: 陳延壽作諸淫巧，日費數萬金。
units.en: Chen Yanshou devised all manner of lewd contrivances, spending tens of thousands in gold every day.
units.literal: Chen Yanshou made all manner of lewd clever devices, spending tens of thousands in gold daily.

units.zh: 宮城左右離宮數十，鋹遊幸常至月餘或旬日。
units.en: Dozens of detached palaces stood on either side of the capital, and Chang's pleasure tours often lasted a month or more, sometimes ten days at a stretch.
units.literal: Several dozen detached palaces stood to left and right of the capital; Chang's excursions often lasted more than a month or ten days at a time.

units.zh: 以豪民為課戶，供宴犒之費。
units.en: Wealthy families were designated tax households to pay for banquets and rewards.
units.literal: Wealthy households were made tax households to supply the costs of feasts and rewards.

units.zh: 乾德中，太祖命師克郴州，獲其內品十餘人。
units.en: During Qiande the Founding Emperor sent troops to take Chen Prefecture and captured more than a dozen of Chang's inner attendants.
units.literal: In the Qiande period the Founding Emperor ordered an army to take Chen Prefecture and captured more than ten of their inner attendants.

units.zh: 有餘延業者，人質麼麽，太祖問曰：「爾在嶺南為何官？」
units.en: Among them was Yu Yanye, a man of slight build and puny stature. The Emperor asked him, "What office did you hold in Lingnan?"
units.literal: Among them was Yu Yanye — a man of meager substance and tiny stature. The Emperor asked, "What office did you hold in Lingnan?"

units.zh: 對曰：「為扈駕弓箭手官。」
units.en: He answered, "I was an officer of the imperial escort archers."
units.literal: He answered: "I was an officer of the escort archers."

units.zh: 命授之弓矢，延業極力控弦不開。
units.en: The Emperor had a bow and arrows handed to him, but Yanye strained with all his might and could not draw the string.
units.literal: The Emperor had a bow and arrows handed him; Yanye strained with all his might but could not draw the bow.

units.zh: 太祖因笑問鋹為治之跡，延業備言其奢酷，太祖驚駭曰：「吾當救此一方之民。」
units.en: The Emperor laughed and asked how Chang governed. Yanye described his extravagance and cruelty in full, and the Emperor cried out in alarm, "I must save the people of that region."
units.literal: The Emperor therefore laughed and asked about Chang's manner of rule; Yanye fully described his extravagance and cruelty; the Emperor cried out in alarm, "I must save the people of this region."

units.zh: 先是，晟因湖南馬氏之亂，襲取桂、郴、賀等州。
units.en: Earlier, Sheng had exploited the turmoil of Hunan's Ma clan to seize Gui, Chen, He, and other prefectures.
units.literal: Earlier, Sheng had taken advantage of disorder in Hunan's Ma clan to seize Gui, Chen, He, and other prefectures.

units.zh: 開寶初，鋹又舉兵侵道州，刺史王繼勳上言。
units.en: Early in Kaibao, Chang again marched against Dao Prefecture, and Prefect Wang Jixun memorialized the throne.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Kaibao era Chang again raised troops to invade Dao Prefecture; prefect Wang Jixun memorialized the throne.

units.zh: 鋹為政昏暴，民被其毒，請討之。
units.en: Chang's rule was benighted and brutal, and the people were suffering under him; he asked that an expedition be launched.
units.literal: Chang's governance was benighted and violent and the people suffered his poison; he asked that they be attacked.

units.zh: 太祖難其事，令江南李煜遣使以書諭鋹使稱臣，歸湖南舊地。
units.en: The Founding Emperor hesitated to act and ordered Li Yu of Jiangnan to send envoys with a letter urging Chang to submit as a vassal and restore the old Hunan territories.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor found the undertaking difficult and ordered Li Yu of Jiangnan to send envoys with a letter urging Chang to submit and return the old territories in Hunan.

units.zh: 鋹不從。
units.en: Chang refused.
units.literal: Chang did not comply.

units.zh: 煜又遣其給事中龔慎儀遺書曰：
units.en: Yu then sent his Supervising Secretary, Gong Shenyi, with another letter that read:
units.literal: Yu again sent his Supervising Secretary Gong Shenyi with a letter saying:

units.zh: 煜與足下叨累世之睦，繼祖考之盟，情若弟兄，義敦交契，憂戚之患，曷嘗不同。
units.en: You and I enjoy the friendship of many generations and inherit the pact our forefathers made. We are as close as brothers, bound by deep obligation, and in joy and sorrow alike — when have we not shared the same fate?
units.literal: Yu and you, sir, enjoy the kindness of many generations and inherit the covenant of our forefathers; our feelings are like those of brothers, our bond of friendship is deep, and in sorrow and joy — when have we not shared alike?

units.zh: 每思會麵而論此懷，抵掌而談此事，交議其所短，各陳其所長；
units.en: I often wish we could meet face to face to speak our minds, clap hands together in debate, each airing the other's faults and each stating his own strengths;
units.literal: I often think of meeting face to face to speak this mind, clapping hands as we discuss these matters, each airing the other's faults and each stating his own strengths;

units.zh: 使中心釋然，利害不惑，而相去萬里，斯願莫伸。
units.en: so that our hearts might be eased and gain and loss made plain — yet we are ten thousand li apart, and this wish cannot be fulfilled.
units.literal: so that the heart might be eased and gain and loss made clear — yet we are ten thousand li apart, and this wish cannot be fulfilled.

units.zh: 凡於事機不得款會，屢達誠素，冀明此心；
units.en: Whenever circumstances denied us a meeting, I wrote again and again in all sincerity, hoping you would see my heart;
units.literal: Whenever affairs did not allow a cordial meeting, I repeatedly expressed my sincere feelings, hoping you would understand this heart;

units.zh: 而足下視之，謂書檄一時之儀，近國梗概之事，外貌而待之，泛濫而觀之，使忠告確論如水投石，若此則又何必事虛詞而勞往復哉？
units.en: Yet you treated them as mere diplomatic formality, scraps of news about a neighboring state — greeting them outwardly and reading them superficially, so that earnest counsel fell like water on stone. If that is so, why trouble with empty words and weary exchanges at all?
units.literal: Yet you, sir, regarded them as mere formal letters of the moment, matters of neighboring states in outline, treating them outwardly and viewing them superficially, so that earnest counsel and solid argument were like water cast on stone — if so, why trouble with empty words and weary exchanges?

units.zh: 殊非宿心之所望也。
units.en: That is far from what I have long hoped for.
units.literal: This is far from what my long-standing heart has hoped for.

units.zh: 今則復遣人使罄申鄙懷，又慮行人失辭，不盡深素，是以再寄翰墨，重布腹心，以代會麵之談與抵掌之議也。
units.en: Now I send another envoy to lay out my thoughts in full, yet I fear he may miss his words and fail to convey what is deepest in me. I therefore write again and lay bare my inmost heart, in place of meeting face to face and debating hand in hand.
units.literal: Now I again send a messenger to express fully my humble feelings, yet fear the envoy may miss his words and not convey my deepest sincerity; therefore I again send this writing and lay bare my inmost heart, in place of face-to-face talk and hand-clapping debate.

units.zh: 足下誠聽其言如交友諫爭之言，視其心如親戚急難之心，然後三復其言，三思其心，則忠乎不忠，斯可見矣，從乎不從，斯可決矣。
units.en: If you truly hear these words as a friend's frank counsel and read this heart as kin in urgent need, then read them three times and ponder my heart three times — whether I am loyal or not will be plain, and whether to heed me or not can be decided.
units.literal: If you, sir, truly hear these words as the remonstrance of a friend and view this heart as the heart of kin in urgent distress, then read them thrice and ponder the heart thrice — whether loyalty or disloyalty will then be plain, and whether to follow or not can then be decided.

units.zh: 昨以大朝南伐，圖復楚疆，交兵已來，遂成釁隙。
units.en: Recently the Great Dynasty marched south to recover Chu territory. Since our armies clashed, a breach has opened between us.
units.literal: Recently the Great Dynasty marched south to recover Chu territory; since arms were joined, a breach has formed.

units.zh: 詳觀事勢，深切憂懷，冀息大朝之兵，求契親仁之願，引領南望，於今累年。
units.en: Watching events closely, I am deeply troubled. I long to see the Great Dynasty's armies stilled and our wish for close, benevolent ties fulfilled. For years now I have strained southward in hope.
units.literal: Observing the situation closely, I am deeply troubled, hoping to still the Great Dynasty's armies and fulfill the wish for close and benevolent ties; stretching my neck southward in longing — for years now.

units.zh: 臨昨使臣入貢大朝，大朝皇帝果以此事宣示曰：「彼若以事大之禮而事我，則何苦而伐之；
units.en: When my envoy went recently to pay tribute to the Great Dynasty, its emperor declared on this very matter: "If they treat me with the deference due a greater power, why should I trouble to attack them?
units.literal: When my envoy went recently to pay tribute to the Great Dynasty, the Great Dynasty's emperor indeed proclaimed on this matter: "If they serve me with the rites of serving the greater power, why must I trouble to attack them?

units.zh: 若欲興戎而爭我，則以必取為度矣。」
units.en: But if they wish to take up arms and fight me, I shall measure success only by total conquest."
units.literal: If they wish to raise arms and contend with me, then I shall measure by certain conquest."

units.zh: 見今點閱大眾，仍以上秋為期，令弊邑以書復敘前意，是用奔走人使，遽貢直言。
units.en: He is mustering his great host even now, with late autumn still set as the deadline, and has ordered my humble state to reply in writing restating our former understanding. That is why I hurry envoys to you and speak frankly without delay.
units.literal: Now he is mustering the great host, still setting late autumn as the deadline, and has ordered my humble state to reply in writing restating the former intent; therefore I hasten envoys and urgently offer frank words.

units.zh: 深料大朝之心非有唯利之貪，蓋怒人之不賓而已；
units.en: I am convinced the Great Dynasty is not driven by greed for gain alone, but by anger that men will not submit;
units.literal: I deeply judge that the Great Dynasty's heart is not moved by greed for profit alone, but anger at men's failure to submit;

units.zh: 足下非有不得已之事與不可易之謀，殆一時之忿而已。
units.en: You have no unavoidable cause and no plan that cannot be changed — this is likely no more than a passing fit of anger.
units.literal: You, sir, have no unavoidable matter and no unalterable plan — it is likely only a moment's anger.

units.zh: 觀夫古之用武者，不顧小大強弱之殊而必戰者有四；
units.en: In antiquity, those who took up arms fought regardless of relative strength in only four circumstances:
units.literal: Observing those who used arms in antiquity, there are four cases in which they fought regardless of differences in size and strength;

units.zh: 父母宗廟之仇，此必戰也；
units.en: vengeance for one's parents and ancestral temple — then one must fight;
units.literal: vengeance for parents and the ancestral temple — in this one must fight;

units.zh: 彼此烏合，民無定心，存亡之機以戰為命，此必戰也；
units.en: when each side is a mere rabble, the people have no settled loyalty, and survival itself depends on fighting — then one must fight;
units.literal: when each side is a mere rabble, the people have no settled heart, and survival or ruin hangs on battle as on life itself — in this one must fight;

units.zh: 敵人有進，必不舍我，求和不得，退守無路，戰亦亡，不戰亦亡，奮不顧命，此必戰也；
units.en: when the enemy presses on and will not let us be, peace is impossible and retreat offers no escape — to fight is death and not to fight is death — then one stakes life without regard and must fight;
units.literal: when the enemy advances and will not spare us, peace cannot be sought, retreat offers no road, to fight is to perish and not to fight is to perish — staking life without regard, in this one must fight;

units.zh: 彼有天亡之兆，我懷進取之機，此必戰也。
units.en: when the foe shows signs that Heaven has doomed him and we hold a chance to advance — then one must fight.
units.literal: when the other has signs of Heaven's doom and we hold a chance to advance — in this one must fight.

units.zh: 今足下與大朝非有父母宗廟之仇也，非同烏合存亡之際也，既殊進退不舍、奮不顧命也，又異乘機進取之時也。
units.en: You and the Great Dynasty bear no feud over parents or ancestral temple. You are not a rabble fighting for survival. You are not trapped with no retreat, staking life in desperation. Nor are you in a moment when Heaven has doomed the foe and you may seize your chance.
units.literal: Now you, sir, and the Great Dynasty have no vengeance for parents and ancestral temple; you are not in the crisis of rabble and survival; you are unlike the case of advance and retreat with no sparing and life staked without regard; you differ again from the time of seizing opportunity to advance.

units.zh: 無故而坐受天下之兵，將決一旦之命，既大朝許以通好，又拒而不從，有國家、利社稷者當若是乎？
units.en: Without cause you would sit and invite the armies of the empire, staking everything on a single throw. The Great Dynasty has offered peace, yet you refuse. Should anyone who cares for his state and altar act thus?
units.literal: Without cause to sit and receive the armies of the empire, staking all on a single throw — when the Great Dynasty has offered peace and you refuse — should one who cares for state and altar act thus?

units.zh: 夫稱帝稱王，角立傑出，今古之常事也；
units.en: To call oneself emperor or king and stand rival among the great has always been common enough;
units.literal: To style oneself emperor or king and stand rival among the outstanding — this is a constant affair of past and present;

units.zh: 割地以通好，玉帛以事人，亦古今之常事也。
units.en: to cede territory for peace and send silks and jades in tribute is equally common in every age.
units.literal: to cede territory to secure peace and offer silks and jades in service to others is also a constant affair of past and present.

units.zh: 盈虛消息、取與翕張，屈伸萬端，在我而已，何必膠柱而用壯，輕禍而爭雄哉？
units.en: Fortune rises and falls, giving and taking expand and contract — the ways to bend and stretch are endless, and the choice is yours alone. Why cling rigidly to force, lightly invite disaster, and fight for supremacy?
units.literal: Fullness and emptiness, waxing and waning, taking and giving, expanding and contracting — the ways of bending and stretching are myriad, and lie in oneself alone; why must one cling to the peg and use force, lightly inviting calamity to contend for supremacy?

units.zh: 且足下以英明之姿，撫百越之眾，北距五嶺，南負重溟，藉累世之基，有及民之澤，眾數十萬，表裏山川，此足下所以慨然而自負也。
units.en: You govern the Hundred Yue with an air of brilliance. The Five Ridges guard you to the north and the deep sea lies to the south. You rest on foundations laid over generations and rule with grace that reaches your people. Your hosts number hundreds of thousands, with mountains and rivers all around. No wonder you feel proud and confident.
units.literal: Moreover, you, sir, with an enlightened bearing govern the peoples of the Hundred Yue; north you hold the Five Ridges, south you lean on the heavy sea; relying on foundations of many generations and possessing grace that reaches the people, your hosts number hundreds of thousands, with mountains and rivers within and without — this is why you, sir, sigh proudly and trust in yourself.

units.zh: 然違天不祥，好戰危事，天方相楚，尚未可爭。
units.en: Yet to defy Heaven brings ill fortune, and love of war is perilous. Heaven now favors Chu, and the time to fight has not come.
units.literal: Yet to defy Heaven is inauspicious, and fondness for war is a perilous affair; Heaven is now favoring Chu, and contention is not yet possible.

units.zh: 恭以大朝師武臣力，實謂天讚也。
units.en: I respectfully hold that the Great Dynasty's martial armies and able ministers are Heaven's own endorsement.
units.literal: I respectfully consider that the Great Dynasty's martial armies and powerful ministers are in truth Heaven's approval.

units.zh: 登太行而伐上黨，士無難色；
units.en: It climbed the Taihang to attack Shangdang, and its soldiers showed no fear;
units.literal: It climbed the Taihang to attack Shangdang, and the soldiers showed no troubled faces;

units.zh: 絕劍閣而舉庸蜀，役不淹時。
units.en: it cut through Jian'ge and conquered Yong and Shu in less than a season.
units.literal: it cut through Jian'ge and raised Yong and Shu, and the campaign did not exceed its season.

units.zh: 是知大朝之力難測也，萬里之境難保也。
units.en: From this you may know the Great Dynasty's strength cannot be measured, and a realm ten thousand li wide cannot be held against it.
units.literal: From this one knows the Great Dynasty's strength is hard to measure and a realm of ten thousand li is hard to preserve.

units.zh: 十戰而九勝，亦一敗可憂；
units.en: Nine victories in ten battles still leave one defeat to dread;
units.literal: Nine victories in ten battles — yet one defeat is cause for worry;

units.zh: 六奇而五中，則一失何補！
units.en: five stratagems succeed out of six — what good does one failure make up for!
units.literal: five hits in six stratagems — what does one miss repair!

units.zh: 況人自以我國險，家自以我兵強，蓋揣於此而不揣於彼，經其成而末經其敗也。
units.en: Moreover, every man trusts his state's rugged terrain and every house trusts its army's strength — they reckon only their own side, not the other, and have known success but not yet defeat.
units.literal: Moreover, each man trusts his state's perilous terrain, each house trusts its army's strength — they reckon this side but not that, have passed through success but not yet through defeat.

units.zh: 何則？
units.en: Why?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 國莫險於劍閣，而庸蜀已亡矣；
units.en: No state was more perilous than at Jian'ge, yet Yong and Shu are already lost;
units.literal: No state was more perilous than at Jian'ge, yet Yong and Shu are already lost;

units.zh: 兵莫強於上黨，而太行不守矣。
units.en: no army was stronger than at Shangdang, yet the Taihang could not be held.
units.literal: no army was stronger than at Shangdang, yet the Taihang could not be held.

units.zh: 人之情，端坐而思之，意滄海可涉也，及風濤驟興，奔舟失馭，與夫坐思之時蓋有殊矣。
units.en: Human nature is such that sitting at ease one imagines the ocean can be crossed; when wind and waves rise suddenly and the boat loses its helm, that is quite another matter from quiet reflection.
units.literal: In human feeling, sitting upright in thought one imagines the blue sea can be crossed; when wind and waves suddenly rise and the fleeing boat loses its helm, it is quite unlike the time of sitting in thought.

units.zh: 是以智者慮於未萌，機者重其先見；
units.en: That is why the wise plan before trouble sprouts, and the quick value foresight;
units.literal: Therefore the wise plan before things sprout, and the quick value foresight;

units.zh: 圖難於其易，居存不忘亡，故曰計禍不及，慮福過之。
units.en: they tackle difficulty while it is still easy and in security do not forget ruin. Hence the saying: we reckon too little for disaster and too much for good fortune.
units.literal: they plot difficulty in its ease and in security do not forget ruin; hence it is said: reckoning of calamity falls short, reckoning of fortune goes too far.

units.zh: 良以福者人之所樂，心樂之，故其望也過；
units.en: For fortune is what men love, and because the heart loves it, hope runs too high;
units.literal: Truly because fortune is what men delight in, the heart delights in it, and therefore hope for it goes too far;

units.zh: 禍者人之所惡，心惡之，故其思也忽。
units.en: calamity is what men hate, and because the heart hates it, thought of it is slight.
units.literal: calamity is what men hate, the heart hates it, and therefore thought of it is slight.

units.zh: 是以福或修於慊望，禍多出於不期。
units.en: Thus good fortune sometimes grows from modest hopes, while disaster often strikes unlooked for.
units.literal: Therefore fortune is sometimes built on modest hope, while calamity often comes unlooked for.

units.zh: 又或慮有矜功好名之臣，獻尊主強國之議者，必曰：「慎無和也。
units.en: You may also hear ministers hungry for glory, urging you to exalt your throne and strengthen your state. They will surely say, "Take care — do not make peace.
units.literal: Again, one may fear ministers who prize merit and love fame, offering counsel to honor the ruler and strengthen the state, who will surely say: "Take care — do not make peace.

units.zh: 五嶺之險，山高水深，輜重不並行，士卒不成列；
units.en: The Five Ridges are perilous — mountains high and waters deep, baggage trains cannot march abreast, and soldiers cannot keep formation;
units.literal: The peril of the Five Ridges — mountains high and waters deep, baggage trains cannot march abreast, soldiers cannot form ranks;

units.zh: 高壘清野而絕其運糧，依山阻水而射以強弩，使進無所得，退無所歸。」
units.en: raise high walls and strip the countryside to cut their supply lines, hold the mountains and waters and shoot them down with powerful crossbows, so that advancing they gain nothing and retreating they have nowhere to go."
units.literal: raise high walls and clear the countryside to cut off their grain transport, rely on mountains and block waters to shoot with powerful crossbows, so that advancing they gain nothing and retreating they have nowhere to return."

units.zh: 此其一也。
units.en: That is the first argument.
units.literal: This is the first argument.

units.zh: 又或曰：「彼所長者，利在平地，今舍其所長，就其所短，雖有百萬之眾，無若我何。」
units.en: Others will say, "Their strength lies on open ground. If we draw them off their strength and fight them in terrain that favors us, even a million men can do nothing against us."
units.literal: Others will say: "Their strength lies on level ground; if we now abandon their strength and meet them in their weakness, though they have a host of a million, they can do nothing to us."

units.zh: 此其二也。
units.en: That is the second.
units.literal: This is the second.

units.zh: 其次或曰：「戰而勝，則霸業可成，戰而不勝，則泛巨舟而浮滄海，終不為人下。」
units.en: Still others will say, "If we fight and win, we can build a hegemony. If we fight and lose, we launch great ships upon the open sea and never bow to another."
units.literal: Next some will say: "If we fight and win, hegemony can be achieved; if we fight and do not win, we launch great ships and float on the blue sea — we shall never be beneath others."

units.zh: 此大約皆說士孟浪之談，謀臣捭闔之策，坐而論之也則易，行之如意也則難。
units.en: These are roughly the reckless talk of itinerant persuaders and the stratagems of scheming ministers — easy to debate at leisure, hard to execute as planned.
units.literal: These are all roughly the reckless talk of persuaders and the stratagems of scheming ministers who open and close — easy to discuss sitting down, hard to carry out as wished.

units.zh: 何則？
units.en: Why?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 今荊湘以南、庸蜀之地，皆是便山水、習險阻之民，不動中國之兵，精卒已逾於十萬矣。
units.en: South of Jing and Xiang and throughout Yong and Shu live peoples at home in mountains and rivers and practiced in rugged terrain. Without even moving the central armies, crack troops already exceed a hundred thousand.
units.literal: Now south of Jing and Xiang and in the lands of Yong and Shu — all are peoples skilled with mountains and waters and practiced in perilous terrain; without moving the armies of the central state, crack troops already exceed a hundred thousand.

units.zh: 況足下與大朝封疆接畛，水陸同途，殆雞犬之相聞，豈馬牛之不及？
units.en: Moreover, your borders touch the Great Dynasty's, with the same routes by land and water — your realms are almost within hearing of each other's dogs and chickens. How could their horses and oxen fail to reach you?
units.literal: Moreover, you, sir, and the Great Dynasty share contiguous borders, with the same routes by water and land — almost within hearing of each other's chickens and dogs; how could horses and oxen not reach?

units.zh: 一旦緣邊悉舉，諸道進攻，豈可俱絕其運糧，盡保其城壁？
units.en: Once frontier posts all rise and armies from every circuit press the attack, how could you cut off every supply line and hold every wall and rampart at once?
units.literal: Once the frontier garrisons all mobilize and every circuit advances in attack, how can one cut off all their grain transport and fully hold every wall and rampart?

units.zh: 若諸險悉固，誠善莫加焉；
units.en: If every strongpoint were fully held, nothing could be better;
units.literal: If every perilous pass were fully secured, nothing finer could be added;

units.zh: 苟尺水橫流，則長堤虛設矣。
units.en: But let a trickle break through anywhere, and the long dike becomes useless.
units.literal: But if a foot's breadth of water flows across, then the long dike is set up for nothing.

units.zh: 其次曰，或大朝用吳越之眾，自泉州泛海以趣國都，則不數日至城下矣。
units.en: The next argument runs that the Great Dynasty might use Wu and Yue troops, sail from Quanzhou across the sea straight toward your capital, and reach your walls within days.
units.literal: The next argument says: Or the Great Dynasty may use the forces of Wu and Yue, sail from Quanzhou across the sea toward the capital, and reach the walls in only a few days.

units.zh: 當其人心疑惑，兵勢動搖，岸上舟中皆為敵國，忠臣義士能復幾人？
units.en: When hearts waver and the army's spirit falters, every shore and every deck becomes enemy ground — how many loyal ministers and steadfast men would remain?
units.literal: When minds are doubtful and the army's morale shakes, shore and ship alike become enemy territory — how many loyal ministers and steadfast men could remain?

units.zh: 懷進退者步步生心，顧妻子者滔滔皆是。
units.en: Men weighing retreat would second-guess every step; men thinking of wives and children would be everywhere.
units.literal: Those weighing advance and retreat harbor second thoughts at every step; those thinking of wives and children are everywhere in torrent.

units.zh: 變故難測，須臾萬端，非惟暫乖始圖，實恐有誤壯誌，又非巨舟之可及，滄海之可遊也。
units.en: Disaster is hard to foresee; in an instant ten thousand things can go wrong — not merely a brief departure from the original plan, but a ruin of grand ambition. And this is no simple matter of launching great ships upon the open sea.
units.literal: Unforeseen turns are hard to foretell; in a moment ten thousand things arise — not only briefly departing from the original plan, but truly fearing harm to grand ambition; and this is not something great ships can reach or the vast sea can be sailed upon.

units.zh: 然此等皆戰伐之常事，兵家之預謀，雖勝負未知，成敗相半。
units.en: Yet these are ordinary matters of war, the sort of plans strategists prepare in advance — victory and defeat unknown, success and failure each as likely as the other.
units.literal: Yet these are all ordinary matters of warfare, plans military strategists prepare in advance — though victory and defeat are unknown, success and failure stand half and half.

units.zh: 苟不得已而為也，固斷在不疑；
units.en: If there is truly no alternative, resolve must be firm and doubtless;
units.literal: If one must do it with no alternative, resolve must be firm and doubtless;

units.zh: 若無大故而思之，又深可痛惜。
units.en: To entertain such thoughts without grave cause is deeply to be lamented.
units.literal: If one considers it without great cause, it is deeply to be lamented.

units.zh: 且小之事大，理固然也。
units.en: Moreover, the lesser serving the greater is the way of nature itself.
units.literal: Moreover, the small serving the great is reason's own requirement.

units.zh: 遠古之例不能備談，本朝當楊氏之建吳也，亦入貢莊宗。
units.en: Ancient precedents are too many to recount, but in our own dynasty, when the Yang clan founded Wu, they too sent tribute to Zhuangzong.
units.literal: Ancient examples cannot all be told; in our dynasty when the Yang clan founded Wu, they also sent tribute to Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 恭自烈祖開基，中原多故，事大之禮，因循未遑，以至交兵，幾成危殆。
units.en: Since our founding ruler opened the realm, the central plains have been in turmoil and the rites owed the greater power were repeatedly deferred — until arms were crossed and our state nearly perished.
units.literal: Respectfully, from the time our founding ruler opened the realm, the central plains had many troubles and the rites of serving the greater power were postponed in neglect, until arms were crossed and peril nearly came to pass.

units.zh: 非不欲憑大江之險，恃眾多之力，尋悟知難則退，遂修出境之盟；
units.en: It was not that we did not wish to rely on the Yangtze's defenses and trust in our numbers; we soon saw the difficulty and withdrew, and then concluded a treaty beyond our borders;
units.literal: It was not that we did not wish to rely on the Yangtze's peril and trust in our numbers; we soon realized difficulty and withdrew, and then concluded a treaty beyond the borders;

units.zh: 一介之使才行，萬里之兵頓息，惠民和眾，於今賴之。
units.en: A single envoy had barely departed when armies ten thousand li away stood down — the people were spared and the realm calmed; to this day we rely on that peace.
units.literal: A single envoy had barely set out when armies ten thousand li away instantly ceased — benefiting the people and harmonizing the masses; to this day we rely on it.

units.zh: 自足下祖德之開基，亦通好中國，以闡霸圖。
units.en: Since your forebears founded your realm, you too have kept friendly ties with the central state to advance your power.
units.literal: From the time your ancestral virtue founded your realm, you too have maintained friendly relations with the central state to advance a hegemonic design.

units.zh: 願修祖宗之謀，以尋中國之好，蕩無益之忿，棄不急之爭；
units.en: I urge you to follow your forebears' design, renew friendship with the central state, sweep away useless anger, and abandon quarrels that need not be fought;
units.literal: I wish you would follow your forebears' design, seek renewed friendship with the central state, sweep away useless anger, and abandon quarrels not urgent;

units.zh: 知存知亡，能強能弱，屈己以濟億兆，談笑而定國家，至德大業無虧也，宗廟社稷無損也。
units.en: Know when to survive and when to perish, when to stand firm and when to yield, bend yourself to save your people, and settle the state with a smile — supreme virtue and great enterprise would suffer no loss, and your ancestral temples and altars no harm.
units.literal: Know survival and destruction, be able to be strong and weak, bend yourself to deliver the hundred million — settle the state with a smile; supreme virtue and great enterprise would suffer no loss, ancestral temples and altars no harm.

units.zh: 玉帛朝聘之禮才出於境，而天下之兵已息矣，豈不易如反掌，固如太山哉？
units.en: Once the rites of tribute and court audience have barely crossed the border, the armies of the empire would stand down — would that not be as easy as turning the hand, as secure as Mount Tai?
units.literal: Once the rites of tribute and court audience have barely left the border, the armies of the empire already cease — would this not be as easy as turning the palm, as firm as Mount Tai?

units.zh: 何必扼腕盱衡，履腸蹀血，然後為勇也。
units.en: Why must one clench one's fist and glare about, tread entrails and wade through blood, before that counts as courage?
units.literal: Why must one clench the wrist and glare about, tread entrails and trample blood, before that counts as courage?

units.zh: 故曰：「德如毛，民鮮克舉之，我儀圖之。」
units.en: Therefore it is said, "Virtue is light as a feather, yet the people can rarely lift it — I will take it as my model."
units.literal: Therefore it is said: "Virtue is like a feather — the people can rarely lift it; I will take it as my model."

units.zh: 又曰：「知止不殆，可以長久。」
units.en: Again it is said, "Knowing when to stop brings no peril; one may endure long."
units.literal: Again it is said: "Knowing when to stop brings no peril; one may endure long."

units.zh: 又曰：「沈潛剛克，高明柔克。」
units.en: Again it is said, "Hidden depth conquers hardness; lofty brightness conquers softness."
units.literal: Again it is said: "Hidden depth conquers hardness; lofty brightness conquers softness."

units.zh: 此聖賢之事業，何恥而不為哉？
units.en: These are the deeds of sages and worthies — what shame could there be in not doing them?
units.literal: These are the achievements of sages — what shame could there be in not doing them?

units.zh: 況大朝皇帝以命世之英，光宅中夏，承五運而乃當正統，度四方則咸偃下風；
units.en: Moreover, the Great Dynasty's emperor is a hero born for the age, illuminating the central lands, inheriting the five cycles and holding the orthodox succession; look to the four quarters and all bow beneath his sway;
units.literal: Moreover, the Great Dynasty's emperor is a hero of the age, illuminating and dwelling in the central lands, inheriting the five cycles and holding the orthodox succession; gauging the four quarters, all bow beneath his wind;

units.zh: 獫狁、太原固不勞於薄伐，南轅返旆更屬在於何人。
units.en: The Xianyun and Taiyuan hardly require a strenuous campaign; for whom else would the imperial chariot wheel south and the banners turn homeward?
units.literal: The Xianyun and Taiyuan surely need no strenuous punitive campaign; who else could the southern chariot wheel turn and the banners return toward?

units.zh: 又方且遏天下之兵鋒，俟貴國之嘉問，則大國之義斯亦以善矣，足下之忿亦可以息矣。
units.en: Moreover, he is now holding back the edge of war across the empire, awaiting a gracious message from your state — then the great state's righteousness would be fulfilled, and your anger could also be stilled.
units.literal: Moreover, he is now restraining the army's edge throughout the empire, awaiting your gracious inquiry — then the great state's righteousness would likewise be fulfilled, and your anger could also be stilled.

units.zh: 若介然不移，有利於宗廟社稷可也，有利於黎元可也，有利於天下可也，有利於身可也。
units.en: If you stand unmoved, it might benefit your ancestral temples and altars, your people, all under Heaven, or even yourself.
units.literal: If you stand unmoved, it may benefit the ancestral temples and altars; it may benefit the common people; it may benefit all under Heaven; it may benefit yourself.

units.zh: 凡是四者無一利焉，何用棄德修怨，自生仇敵，使赫赫南國，將成禍機，炎炎奈何，其可向邇？
units.en: Yet of these four, not one would gain — why abandon virtue and nurture enmity, create enemies yourself, and let your glorious southern state become a seed of disaster? With such blazing peril, how could one draw near?
units.literal: Yet of these four, not one would gain — why abandon virtue and nurture enmity, create enemies yourself, and let your glorious southern state become a seed of calamity? Blazing heat — how could one draw near?

units.zh: 幸而小勝也，莫保其後焉，不幸而違心，則大事去矣。
units.en: Even a small victory could not secure what follows; if fortune turns against you, the great affair is lost.
units.literal: Even if fortunate in a small victory, one cannot secure what follows; if unlucky and against the heart's wish, the great affair is lost.

units.zh: 復念頃者淮、泗交兵，疆陲多壘，吳越以累世之好，遂首為厲階；
units.en: Again I recall how recently armies clashed at Huai and Si, the borders bristled with forts, and Wu and Yue — despite generations of friendship — became the first to open the way to disaster;
units.literal: Again I think how recently armies clashed at Huai and Si, the borders bristled with forts, and Wu and Yue — despite generations of friendship — became the first to lead the way to disaster;

units.zh: 惟有貴國情分逾親，歡盟愈篤，在先朝感義，情實慨然，下走承基，理難負德，不能自己，又馳此緘。
units.en: Only your state has been bound to us by ever closer ties and ever deeper alliance. The former court was moved by righteousness and felt true indignation; I who have inherited the throne can hardly betray such virtue — unable to restrain myself, I send this letter once more.
units.literal: Only your honorable state has been bound by ever closer feeling and ever deeper alliance. The former court was moved by righteousness and felt true indignation; I who have inherited the throne can hardly betray such virtue — unable to restrain myself, I send this letter again.

units.zh: 近奉大朝諭旨，以為足下無通好之心，必舉上秋之役，即命弊邑速絕連盟。
units.en: Recently I received an edict from the Great Dynasty stating that you, sir, have no mind for renewed friendship and will surely resume last autumn's campaign; it ordered our humble state at once to sever our alliance.
units.literal: Recently I received an edict from the Great Dynasty, holding that you, sir, have no mind for renewed friendship and will surely launch the autumn campaign of last year; it ordered our humble state at once to sever our alliance.

units.zh: 雖善鄰之心，期於永保；
units.en: Though our wish for good neighborliness hoped to preserve it forever;
units.literal: Though the heart of good neighborliness hoped to preserve it forever;

units.zh: 而事大之節，焉敢固違。
units.en: yet the duty owed the greater power — how could we stubbornly refuse?
units.literal: the propriety of serving the greater power — how dare we obstinately defy it?

units.zh: 恐煜之不得事足下也，是以惻惻之意所不能雲，區區之誠於是乎在。
units.en: I fear that Yu may no longer serve you, sir — hence the anguish I cannot put into words; my humble sincerity lies in this letter.
units.literal: I fear Yu may no longer serve you, sir — hence the anguish I cannot put into words; my humble sincerity lies here.

units.zh: 又念臣子之情，尚不逾於三諫，煜之極言，於此三矣，是為臣者可以逃，為子者可以泣，為交友者亦惆悵而遂絕矣。
units.en: Again I reflect that the bond between subject and ruler does not extend beyond three remonstrances — Yu has spoken to the utmost, now three times. A subject may flee, a son may weep, a friend may grieve and break off — and so it must be.
units.literal: Again I reflect that the feeling between subject and ruler does not go beyond three remonstrances — Yu has spoken to the utmost, now three times. A subject may flee, a son may weep, a friend may grieve and break off — and so it must be.

units.zh: 鋹得書，遂囚慎儀，驛書答煜，言甚不遜，煜上其書。
units.en: Chang received the letter, imprisoned Shen Yi, and answered Yu by courier in terms most insolent; Yu forwarded the letter to the throne.
units.literal: Chang received the letter, thereupon imprisoned Shen Yi, and answered Yu by courier with words most insolent; Yu forwarded the letter to the throne.

units.zh: 開寶三年，太祖命潭州防禦使潘美、朗州團練使尹崇珂討之。
units.en: In the third year of Kaibao, Taizu ordered Pan Mei, defender of Tan, and Yin Chongke, training commissioner of Lang, to campaign against him.
units.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, Taizu ordered Pan Mei, defender of Tan Prefecture, and Yin Chongke, training commissioner of Lang Prefecture, to campaign against him.

units.zh: 八月，師至白霞，
units.en: In the eighth month the army arrived at Baixia,
units.literal: In the eighth month the army reached Baixia,

units.zh: 鋹賀州刺史陳守忠告急於鋹。
units.en: and Chen Shouzhong, Chang's prefect of He, reported the emergency to him.
units.literal: and Chen Shouzhong, prefect of He Prefecture under Chang, reported the emergency to Chang.

units.zh: 時舊將多以讒構誅死，宗室翦滅殆盡，掌兵者唯宦人數輩。
units.en: By then many veteran generals had been executed on slander; the imperial clan was nearly wiped out; only a handful of eunuchs held military authority.
units.literal: At that time many veteran generals had been executed on slander; the imperial clan was nearly exterminated; those holding military authority were only a few eunuchs.

units.zh: 自晟以來，耽於遊宴，城壁壕隍多飾為宮館池沼，樓艦皆毀，兵器又腐，內外震恐。
units.en: Since Shen's time he had indulged in feasts and revelry; city walls and moats were largely turned into palaces, lodges, and ponds; tower ships were destroyed and weapons left to rot — within and without, all were shaken with fear.
units.literal: Since Shen's time he had indulged in feasts and revelry; city walls and moats were largely decorated into palaces, lodges, and ponds; tower ships were all destroyed and weapons rotted — within and without, all were shaken with fear.

units.zh: 乃遣龔澄樞往賀州，郭崇嶽往桂州，李托往韶州，畫守禦之策。
units.en: He then sent Gong Chengshu to He, Guo Chongyue to Gui, and Li Tuo to Shao to devise defensive plans.
units.literal: He then sent Gong Chengshu to He Prefecture, Guo Chongyue to Gui Prefecture, and Li Tuo to Shao Prefecture to devise defensive plans.

units.zh: 九月，美與崇珂圍賀州，澄樞遁歸。
units.en: In the ninth month Mei and Chongke besieged He Prefecture; Chengshu fled home.
units.literal: In the ninth month Mei and Chongke besieged He Prefecture; Chengshu fled back.

units.zh: 鋹遣大將伍彥柔領兵赴賀，美等以奇兵伏南鄉岸。
units.en: Chang sent the great general Wu Yanrou with troops to relieve He; Mei and the others laid ambush troops on the southern bank.
units.literal: Chang sent the great general Wu Yanrou with troops to relieve He; Mei and the others set ambush troops on the southern bank.

units.zh: 彥柔夜至，艤舟岸側，遲明挾彈登岸，踞胡床指麾。
units.en: Yanrou arrived by night, moored his boats along the shore, and at dawn came ashore with a crossbow, seated on a folding camp chair to direct the battle.
units.literal: Yanrou arrived by night, moored boats along the shore, and at dawn came ashore with a crossbow, seated on a folding camp chair to command.

units.zh: 伏兵卒發，彥柔眾大亂，死者千人。
units.en: The ambush sprang; Yanrou's force fell into chaos, and a thousand men died.
units.literal: The ambush suddenly sprang; Yanrou's force fell into great disorder, and a thousand died.

units.zh: 擒彥柔斬之，梟首以示城中。
units.en: They captured Yanrou and beheaded him, displaying his head before the city.
units.literal: They captured Yanrou and beheaded him, displaying the head before the city.

units.zh: 翌日，城陷。
units.en: The following day the city was taken.
units.literal: The next day the city fell.

units.zh: 美等督戰艦，聲言順流趨廣州，鋹令都統潘崇徹將兵五萬屯賀江。
units.en: Mei and the others led the war fleet, proclaiming they would sail downstream toward Guangzhou; Chang ordered Commander-in-Chief Pan Chongche to lead fifty thousand troops to encamp on the He River.
units.literal: Mei and the others commanded war vessels, proclaiming they would sail downstream toward Guangzhou; Chang ordered the commander-in-chief Pan Chongche to lead fifty thousand troops to encamp on the He River.

units.zh: 十月，美等次昭州，破開建砦，殺卒數百，擒砦將靳暉，昭州刺史田行稠遁去，城遂陷。
units.en: In the tenth month Mei and the others reached Zhao Prefecture, broke Kaijian Fort, killed several hundred soldiers, and captured the fort commander Jin Hui; Zhao Prefect Tian Xingchou fled and the city fell.
units.literal: In the tenth month Mei and the others halted at Zhao Prefecture, broke Kaijian Fort, killed several hundred soldiers, captured the fort commander Jin Hui; Tian Xingchou, prefect of Zhao, fled and the city fell.

units.zh: 桂州刺史李承進棄城亦奔。
units.en: Gui Prefect Li Chengjin abandoned the city and fled as well.
units.literal: Li Chengjin, prefect of Gui, abandoned the city and fled as well.

units.zh: 十一月，連州陷，招討使盧收率眾退保清遠。
units.en: In the eleventh month Lian Prefecture fell; Pacification Commissioner Lu Shou withdrew his forces to hold Qingyuan.
units.literal: In the eleventh month Lian Prefecture fell; the pacification commissioner Lu Shou led his forces back to hold Qingyuan.

units.zh: 十二月，美等攻韶州，都統李承渥以兵數萬陣蓮華山下。
units.en: In the twelfth month Mei and the others attacked Shao Prefecture; Commander-in-Chief Li Chengwo drew up an army of tens of thousands below Lianhua Mountain.
units.literal: In the twelfth month Mei and the others attacked Shao Prefecture; the commander-in-chief Li Chengwo drew up an army of tens of thousands below Lianhua Mountain.

units.zh: 初，鋹教象為陣，每象載十數人，皆執兵仗，凡戰必置陣前，以壯軍威。
units.en: Earlier Chang had trained elephants for battle; each elephant carried a dozen armed men and was placed at the front of every formation to bolster the army's prestige.
units.literal: Earlier Chang had trained elephants into formation; each elephant bore a dozen men all holding weapons; in every battle they were placed before the line to bolster the army's prestige.

units.zh: 至是與美遇，美盡索軍中勁弩布前以射之，象奔踶，乘象者皆墜，反踐承渥軍，遂大敗，承渥僅以身免。
units.en: Now they met Mei, who gathered every powerful crossbow in the army and arrayed them forward to shoot; the elephants stampeded, their riders fell, and they trampled Chengwo's army in turn — utter defeat; Chengwo barely escaped with his life.
units.literal: Now they met Mei; Mei gathered every powerful crossbow in the army and arrayed them forward to shoot; the elephants ran and stamped, riders all fell, and trampled Chengwo's army in reverse — utter defeat; Chengwo barely escaped with his life.

units.zh: 韶州陷，擒刺史辛延渥、諫議大夫卿文遠。
units.en: Shao Prefecture fell; Prefect Xin Yanwo and Remonstrance Grandee Qing Wenyuan were captured.
units.literal: Shao Prefecture fell; the prefect Xin Yanwo and remonstrance grandee Qing Wenyuan were captured.

units.zh: 鋹始令塹廣州東壕，遣郭崇嶽統兵六萬屯馬逕，列柵以拒之。
units.en: Chang at last ordered trenches dug along Guangzhou's eastern moat and sent Guo Chongyue to command sixty thousand troops at Majing, setting palisades to resist.
units.literal: Chang at last ordered trenches dug along Guangzhou's eastern moat and sent Guo Chongyue to command sixty thousand troops encamped at Majing, setting palisades to resist.

units.zh: 四年正月，美等破英、雄二州，都統潘崇徹來降。
units.en: In the first month of the fourth year Mei and the others took Ying and Xiong prefectures; Commander-in-Chief Pan Chongche surrendered.
units.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Mei and the others took Ying and Xiong prefectures; Commander-in-Chief Pan Chongche came over in surrender.

units.zh: 翌日，次瀧頭，鋹遣使請和，且求緩師。
units.en: The next day they halted at Longtou; Chang sent envoys to sue for peace and ask that the advance be slowed.
units.literal: The next day they halted at Longtou; Chang sent envoys to sue for peace and ask that the army be slowed.

units.zh: 瀧頭山水險惡，美等疑有伏兵，乃挾鋹使速度諸險。
units.en: Longtou's terrain was rugged and perilous; Mei and the others suspected ambush and forced Chang's envoy to hurry them through the dangerous passes.
units.literal: Longtou's mountains and waters were perilous and harsh; Mei and the others suspected ambush and therefore forced Chang's envoy to speed them through the dangerous passes.

units.zh: 二月，過馬逕，去廣城十里，砦於雙女山下。
units.en: In the second month they passed Majing, ten li from the capital, and encamped below Shuangnv Mountain.
units.literal: In the second month they passed Majing, ten li from Guang City, and encamped below Shuangnv Mountain.

units.zh: 鋹聞之，取舶船十餘艘，載金寶、妃嬪欲入海。
units.en: When Chang heard of it, he took more than ten ocean-going ships, loaded them with gold, treasures, and concubines, and prepared to flee to sea.
units.literal: Chang heard of it, took more than ten ocean-going ships, loaded gold and treasures and concubines, intending to flee to sea.

units.zh: 未及發，宦官樂範與衛兵千餘盜舶船走。
units.en: Before they could depart, the eunuch Yue Fan and more than a thousand guards stole the ships and fled.
units.literal: Before they could depart, the eunuch Yue Fan and over a thousand guards stole the ships and fled.

units.zh: 美等將至城，鋹懼，遣其右僕射蕭漼奉表詣軍門乞降。
units.en: As Mei and the others were about to reach the city, Chang in fear sent his Right Vice Director Xiao Hun to present a memorial at the army gate begging to surrender.
units.literal: As Mei and the others were about to reach the city, Chang in fear sent his Right Vice Director Xiao Hun to present a memorial at the army gate begging surrender.

units.zh: 美諭太祖意，語在《美傳》。
units.en: Mei conveyed Taizu's intent — the account appears in Mei's biography.
units.literal: Mei expounded Taizu's intent — the account is in the Biography of Mei.

units.zh: 使者乞部送赴闕，師遂頓城外。
units.en: The envoy asked to be escorted to the capital; the army thereupon halted outside the city.
units.literal: The envoy asked to be escorted to court; the army thereupon halted outside the walls.

units.zh: 鋹又遣其弟保興率百官奉迎，為郭崇嶽所遏。
units.en: Chang again sent his younger brother Baoxing leading the officials to welcome them, but Guo Chongyue blocked them.
units.literal: Chang again sent his younger brother Baoxing leading the hundred officials to welcome them, but they were blocked by Guo Chongyue.

units.zh: 崇嶽無謀勇，但祈禱鬼神，復為拒捍之備。
units.en: Chongyue lacked strategy and courage; he only prayed to spirits and gods and again prepared to resist.
units.literal: Chongyue lacked strategy and courage; he only prayed to spirits and gods and again made preparations to resist.

units.zh: 美等乃進攻，保興迎戰，大為所敗，美乘風縱火，煙埃坌起，崇嶽死於亂兵。
units.en: Mei and the others then pressed the attack; Baoxing met them in battle and was utterly defeated. Mei took the wind to set fires; smoke and dust billowed up; Chongyue died in the melee.
units.literal: Mei and the others then pressed the attack; Baoxing met them in battle and was utterly defeated. Mei took the wind to set fires; smoke and dust billowed up; Chongyue died among the disorderly troops.

units.zh: 城既破，鋹盡焚其府庫。
units.en: Once the city fell, Chang burned all the treasuries.
units.literal: Once the city was broken, Chang burned all the treasuries.

units.zh: 美擒鋹及龔澄樞、李托、薛崇譽與宗室文武九十七人，同縻於龍德宮。
units.en: Mei captured Chang along with Gong Chengshu, Li Tuo, Xue Chongyu, and ninety-seven members of the imperial clan and the civil and military elite, all held together in Longde Palace.
units.literal: Mei captured Chang together with Gong Chengshu, Li Tuo, Xue Chongyu, and ninety-seven members of the imperial clan and civil and military officials, all confined together in Longde Palace.

units.zh: 保興逃於民家，亦獲之，悉部送闕下。
units.en: Baoxing hid in a commoner's home but was also captured; all were escorted to court.
units.literal: Baoxing hid in a commoner's home but was also taken; all were escorted to court.

units.zh: 斬閹工五百餘人。
units.en: More than five hundred eunuch craftsmen were beheaded.
units.literal: More than five hundred castrated palace artisans were beheaded.

units.zh: 凡得州六十、縣二百十四、戶十七萬。
units.en: In all they took sixty prefectures, two hundred fourteen counties, and one hundred seventy thousand households.
units.literal: In all they obtained sixty prefectures, two hundred fourteen counties, and one hundred seventy thousand households.

units.zh: 鋹至江陵，邸吏龐師進迎謁，學士黃德昭侍鋹，鋹問師進何人，德昭曰：「本國人也。」
units.en: When Chang reached Jiangling, lodge clerk Pang Shijin came to greet him; academician Huang Dezhao attended Chang, who asked who Shijin was; Dezhao said, "He is a man of our own state."
units.literal: When Chang reached Jiangling, lodge clerk Pang Shijin came to greet and pay respects; academician Huang Dezhao attended Chang, who asked who Shijin was; Dezhao said: "He is a man of our own state."

units.zh: 鋹曰：「何為在此？」
units.en: Chang said, "Why is he here?"
units.literal: Chang said: "Why is he here?"

units.zh: 曰：「先主歲貢大朝，輜重比至荊州，乃令師進至邸，於此造車，以給饋運爾。」
units.en: He said, "The former ruler sent yearly tribute to the Great Dynasty; when the baggage train reached Jingzhou, Shijin was posted to the lodge here to build carts for the supply transport — that is all."
units.literal: He said: "The former ruler yearly sent tribute to the Great Dynasty; when the baggage train reached Jingzhou, Shijin was posted to the lodge here to build carts to supply the transport — that is all."

units.zh: 鋹歎曰：「我在位十四年，未嘗聞此言，今日始知祖宗山河及大朝境土也。」
units.en: Chang sighed, "In my fourteen years on the throne I never heard this — today I first learn the extent of our forebears' realm and the Great Dynasty's territory."
units.literal: Chang sighed: "In my fourteen years on the throne I never heard this — today I first learn of our forebears' mountains and rivers and the Great Dynasty's territory."

units.zh: 因泣涕久之。
units.en: He wept for a long time.
units.literal: Thereupon he wept for a long while.

units.zh: 至京，舍於玉津園，太祖遣參知政事呂餘慶問鋹翻覆及焚府庫之罪，鋹歸罪澄樞、托、崇譽。
units.en: When he reached the capital he was lodged at Yujin Garden; Taizu sent Vice Grand Councilor Lu Yuqing to question him about his treachery and the burning of the treasuries, and Chang blamed Chengshu, Tuo, and Chongyu.
units.literal: Upon reaching the capital he was lodged at Yujin Garden; Taizu sent Vice Grand Councilor Lu Yuqing to question Chang on his treachery and the burning of the treasuries; Chang blamed Chengshu, Tuo, and Chongyu.

units.zh: 翌日，有司以帛係鋹及其官屬獻太廟、太社。
units.en: The next day the responsible offices bound Chang and his officials with silk cords and presented them before the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Altar of Soil and Grain.
units.literal: The next day the responsible offices bound Chang and his officials with silk cords and presented them at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Altar of Soil and Grain.

units.zh: 太祖禦明德門，遣攝刑部尚書盧多遜宣詔責鋹，鋹對曰：「臣年十六僭偽位，澄樞等皆先臣舊人，每事臣不得專，在國時臣是臣下，澄樞是國主。」
units.en: Taizu took his seat at the Gate of Bright Virtue and dispatched Acting Minister of Justice Lu Duoxun to proclaim the edict reproaching Chang; Chang replied, "Your subject at sixteen usurped a false throne; Chengshu and the others were all my father's old retainers — in every matter I could not decide alone. In the state I was the subject and Chengshu was the sovereign."
units.literal: Taizu took the seat at Gate of Bright Virtue and dispatched Acting Minister of Justice Lu Duoxun to proclaim the edict reproaching Chang; Chang replied: "Your subject at sixteen usurped a false throne; Chengshu and the others were all my father's old retainers — in every matter I could not decide alone. While in the state I was the subject and Chengshu was the sovereign."

units.zh: 遂伏地待罪。
units.en: He then prostrated himself to await judgment.
units.literal: Thereupon he prostrated himself to await judgment.

units.zh: 太祖命攝大理卿高繼申引澄樞、托、崇譽斬於千秋門外。
units.en: Taizu ordered Acting Chief Justice Gao Jishen to lead Chengshu, Tuo, and Chongyu out and behead them outside the Gate of a Thousand Autumns.
units.literal: Taizu ordered Acting Chief Justice Gao Jishen to lead out Chengshu, Tuo, and Chongyu and behead them outside the Gate of a Thousand Autumns.

units.zh: 釋鋹罪，賜襲衣、冠帶、器幣、鞍勒馬，授金紫光祿大夫、檢校太保、右千牛衛大將軍、員外置同正員，封恩赦侯，朝會班上將軍之下。
units.en: He pardoned Chang, bestowed formal robes, cap and belt, ritual objects, and a saddled horse, appointed him Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, Acting Grand Guardian, General of the Right Palace Guard Cavalry, with extra-staff status equal to regular appointment, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gracious Pardon, ranking in court assemblies below full generals.
units.literal: He released Chang from punishment, bestowed formal robes, cap and belt, ritual objects, and a saddled horse, appointed him Grandee of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, Acting Grand Guardian, General of the Right Palace Guard Cavalry, with extra-staff status equal to regular appointment, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gracious Pardon, ranking in court assemblies below full generals.

units.zh: 以其弟保興為右監門率府率，左僕射蕭漼為太子中允，中書舍人卓惟休為太僕寺丞，餘並署諸州上佐、縣令、主簿。
units.en: His younger brother Baoxing was made Colonel of the Right Gate Guard; Left Vice Director Xiao Hun was made Principal in the Crown Prince's household; Drafting Attendant Zhuo Weiqiu was made Assistant Director of the Imperial Stud — the rest were assigned as senior aides in prefectures, magistrates, and clerks.
units.literal: His younger brother Baoxing was made Colonel of the Right Gate Guard; Left Vice Director Xiao Hun was made Principal in the Crown Prince's household; Drafting Attendant Zhuo Weiqiu was made Assistant Director of the Imperial Stud — the rest were all assigned as senior aides in prefectures, magistrates, and clerks.

units.zh: 初，龑時嘗召司天監周傑筮之，遇《復》之《豐》，龑問曰：「享年幾何？」
units.en: Earlier, in the time of the emperor with the invented name, Director of the Astronomical Bureau Zhou Jie was summoned to divine by the Book of Changes; he obtained Hexagram Fu (Return) changing to Feng (Abundance). That ruler asked, "How many years will the dynasty endure?"
units.literal: Earlier, in the time of the emperor with the invented name, the Director of the Astronomical Bureau Zhou Jie was summoned to divine by the Book of Changes; he obtained Hexagram Fu (Return) changing to Feng (Abundance). That ruler asked: "How many years will the dynasty endure?"

units.zh: 傑曰：「凡二卦皆土為應，土之數五，二五，十也，上下各五，將五百五十五乎。」
units.en: Jie said, "In both hexagrams earth is the corresponding line; earth's number is five — two fives make ten; upper and lower each five — will it be five hundred fifty-five?"
units.literal: Jie said: "In both hexagrams earth is the corresponding line; earth's number is five — two fives make ten; upper and lower each five — will it be five hundred fifty-five?"

units.zh: 及鋹之敗，果五十五年，蓋傑舉成數以避一時之害爾。
units.en: When Chang fell it was indeed fifty-five years — Jie had given a round number to escape immediate harm.
units.literal: When Chang was defeated it was indeed fifty-five years — Jie had cited a round number to escape immediate harm.

units.zh: 又廣州童謠曰：「羊頭二四，白天雨至。」
units.en: A children's rhyme also circulated in Guangzhou: "Sheep's head, two-four — by day the heavenly rain arrives."
units.literal: There was also a children's rhyme in Guangzhou: "Sheep's head, two-four — by day the heavenly rain arrives."

units.zh: 識者以羊是未之神，是歲歲在辛未，以二月四日擒鋹。
units.en: Those who interpreted omens held that sheep corresponds to the sign wei; that year was xinwei, and on the fourth day of the second month Chang was captured.
units.literal: Those who interpreted signs held that sheep corresponds to the sign wei; that year was xinwei, and on the second month's fourth day Chang was captured.

units.zh: 天雨者，王師如時雨之義。
units.en: "Heavenly rain" meant the royal army coming like timely rain.
units.literal: "Heavenly rain" meant the royal army like timely rain.

units.zh: 又前一年九月八日夕，眾星皆北流，有知星者言，劉氏歸朝之兆也。
units.en: Also on the evening of the eighth day of the ninth month the year before, all the stars flowed northward; one versed in stars said it was an omen of the Liu house returning to the court.
units.literal: Also on the evening of the eighth day of the ninth month the year before, all stars flowed northward; one versed in stars said it was an omen of the Liu house returning to the court.

units.zh: 四年，詔鋹月給增錢五萬、米麥五十斛。
units.en: In the fourth year an edict raised Chang's monthly stipend by fifty thousand cash and fifty hu of millet and wheat.
units.literal: In the fourth year an edict increased Chang's monthly stipend by fifty thousand cash and fifty hu of millet and wheat.

units.zh: 八年，李煜平，遷左監門衛上將軍，進封彭城郡公。
units.en: In the eighth year, after Li Yu's realm was pacified, he was made General-in-Chief of the Left Gate Guard and advanced to Duke of Pengcheng commandery.
units.literal: In the eighth year, after Li Yu's realm was pacified, he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Gate Guard and advanced to Duke of Pengcheng commandery.

units.zh: 太平興國初，又進衛國公。
units.en: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was further promoted to Duke of Weiguo.
units.literal: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was further advanced to Duke of Weiguo.

units.zh: 五年，卒，年三十九。
units.en: In the fifth year he died at the age of thirty-nine.
units.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged thirty-nine.

units.zh: 廢朝三日，贈太師，追封南越王。
units.en: Court was suspended for three days in mourning; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as King of Southern Yue.
units.literal: Court mourning was suspended for three days; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as King of Southern Yue.

units.zh: 鋹體質豐碩，眉目俱竦。
units.en: Chang was a large, heavyset man with keen, alert eyes and brows.
units.literal: Chang's physique was ample and stout; his eyes and brows were both sharp-set.

units.zh: 有口辯，性絕巧，嘗以珠結鞍勒為戲龍之狀，極其精妙，以獻太祖。
units.en: He was quick with words and possessed extraordinary craftsmanship. Once he fashioned saddle trappings from pearls in the shape of a frolicking dragon with exquisite skill and presented them to Taizu.
units.literal: He had eloquence in speech and a nature of surpassing skill; once he strung pearls into saddle trappings in the form of a playful dragon, to the utmost refinement, and presented them to Taizu.

units.zh: 太祖詔示諸宮官，皆駭伏，遂以錢百五十萬給其直，謂左右臣曰：「鋹好工巧，習以成性，儻能以習巧之勤移於治國，豈至滅亡哉！」
units.en: Taizu displayed the work to the palace officials, who were all struck with wonder. He paid one million five hundred thousand cash for it and told his attendants, "Chang loves craftsmanship so deeply that it has become second nature to him. If he had applied that same diligence to governing his state, how could he have fallen?"
units.literal: Taizu had it shown to the palace officials; all were awed and subdued. He then gave one million five hundred thousand cash as its price and said to the ministers at his side: "Chang loves craftsmanship until it has become his nature — if he could transfer the diligence he spends on skill to governing the state, how would he have come to ruin!"

units.zh: 太祖嘗乘肩輿從十數騎幸講武池，從官未集，鋹先至，賜鋹卮酒。
units.en: Once Taizu went in a sedan chair with a dozen mounted attendants to the Drill Pool. His retinue had not yet gathered when Chang arrived ahead of them, and Taizu offered him a cup of wine.
units.literal: Taizu once rode in a sedan chair with a dozen-odd mounted followers to visit the Drill Pool; the attendants had not yet assembled when Chang arrived first, and Taizu granted Chang a cup of wine.

units.zh: 鋹疑為冘，泣曰：「臣承祖父基業，違拒韓廷，勞王師致討，罪固當死，陛下不殺臣，今見太平，為大梁布衣足矣。
units.en: Chang feared it was poisoned wine and wept, saying, "Your subject inherited my grandfather's realm, defied the Han court, and brought the imperial army down upon me — a crime that surely deserved death. Your Majesty spared my life; now that I live to see peace, it is enough to be an ordinary subject of Great Liang.
units.literal: Chang suspected it was poisoned wine and wept, saying: "Your subject inherited my grandfather's enterprise, defied the Han court, and taxed the royal army to campaign against me — the crime surely deserved death. Your Majesty did not kill me; now I behold peace, and to be a common cloth-clad man of Great Liang is enough.

units.zh: 願延旦夕之命，以全陛下生成之恩，臣未敢飲此酒。」
units.en: I beg only to live out my days and honor Your Majesty's mercy in sparing me. I dare not drink this wine."
units.literal: I wish to extend my life day by day, to fulfill Your Majesty's grace in giving me life — your subject dare not drink this wine."

units.zh: 太祖笑曰：「朕推心於人腹，安有此事！」
units.en: Taizu laughed and said, "I give men my full trust — how could I do such a thing!"
units.literal: Taizu laughed and said: "I lay my heart open in men's breasts — how could there be such a thing!"

units.zh: 命取鋹酒自飲之，別酌以賜，鋹大慚頓首謝。
units.en: He had Chang's cup brought and drank from it himself, then poured a fresh cup for Chang. Deeply ashamed, Chang kowtowed in gratitude.
units.literal: He ordered Chang's wine taken and drank it himself, then poured another cup to grant him; Chang was deeply ashamed and prostrated himself in thanks.

units.zh: 太宗將討晉陽，召近臣宴，鋹預之，自言：「朝廷威靈及遠，四方僭竊之主，今日盡在坐中，旦夕平太原，劉繼元又至，臣率先來朝，願得執梃為諸國降王長。」
units.en: When Taizong prepared to attack Jinyang, he summoned his close ministers to a banquet at which Chang was present. Chang declared, "The court's authority reaches to the farthest corners — every usurping ruler in the realm is seated here tonight. Taiyuan will fall any day now, and Liu Jiyuan will follow. Your subject was the first to submit; let me lead the procession of surrendered kings with staff in hand."
units.literal: Taizong was about to campaign against Jinyang and summoned close ministers to a banquet; Chang was among them and spoke on his own: "The court's majesty and spirit reach far — all the usurping lords of the four directions are today gathered at this banquet. Taiyuan will soon be pacified and Liu Jiyuan will arrive next. Your subject came to court first and wishes to take the staff as chief among the surrendered kings of the various states."

units.zh: 太宗大笑，賞賜甚厚。
units.en: Taizong roared with laughter and rewarded him handsomely.
units.literal: Taizong laughed greatly and rewarded him very generously.

units.zh: 其詼諧此類也。
units.en: His humor ran in this vein.
units.literal: His wit and humor were of this sort.

units.zh: 鋹子守節、守正，皆至崇儀副使。
units.en: Chang's sons Shoujie and Shouzheng both rose to Deputy Commissioner of Chongyi.
units.literal: Chang's sons Shoujie and Shouzheng both reached the post of Deputy Commissioner of Chongyi.

units.zh: 守正卒，帝聞其家貧，詔月給萬錢。
units.en: When Shouzheng died, the Emperor learned that his family was destitute and ordered a monthly stipend of ten thousand cash.
units.literal: Shouzheng died; the Emperor heard that his household was poor and issued an edict granting ten thousand cash monthly.

units.zh: 守素，咸平中為侍禁，亦貧，真宗賜白金百兩，語宰相曰：「諸偽主子孫率多窘迫，蓋僭侈之後不知稼穡艱難所致也。」
units.en: Shousu served as a Palace Attendant during the Xianping era and was likewise impoverished. Zhenzong granted him one hundred taels of silver and told the chief ministers, "The descendants of the former usurping rulers are mostly in want — bred to extravagance, they never learned the labor that fills the granary."
units.literal: Shousu, in the Xianping era, served as Palace Attendant and was also poor; Zhenzong bestowed one hundred taels of white gold and told the chief ministers: "The sons and grandsons of the various false lords are mostly in straitened circumstances — after lives of extravagant usurpation they do not know the hardship of farming."

units.zh: 後至內殿崇班，天禧中，又錄為閣門祗候。
units.en: He later rose to the Inner Hall Honored Class, and in the Tianxi era was appointed Gate Attendant.
units.literal: Later he reached the Inner Hall Honored Class; in the Tianxi era he was again enrolled as Gate Attendant.

units.zh: 守通，供奉官。
units.en: Shoutong served as a Tribute Official.
units.literal: Shoutong was a Tribute Official.

units.zh: 守正子克昌，為三班奉職；
units.en: Shouzheng's son Kechang held the rank of Third-Rank Attendant;
units.literal: Shouzheng's son Kechang was a Third-Rank Attendant;

units.zh: 國昌，為借職。
units.en: Guochang held only a provisional acting commission.
units.literal: Guochang was granted a borrowed (acting) office.

units.zh: 龔澄樞，廣州南海人。
units.en: Gong Chengshu came from Nanhai in Guangzhou.
units.literal: Gong Chengshu was a native of Nanhai in Guangzhou.

units.zh: 性廉謹，不妄交遊。
units.en: He was upright and cautious by nature and kept few companions.
units.literal: His character was honest and careful; he did not socialize casually.

units.zh: 幼事龑為內供奉官，累遷內給事。
units.en: In his youth he entered service under the emperor with the invented name as an Inner Tribute Official and rose through successive posts to Inner Provisioner.
units.literal: In youth he served the emperor with the invented name as Inner Tribute Official and was repeatedly promoted to Inner Provisioner.

units.zh: 晟襲位，任閹人林延遇為甘泉宮使，頗預政事。
units.en: When Shen took the throne, he made the eunuch Lin Yanyu Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, and Lin came to wield considerable influence over state affairs.
units.literal: When Shen succeeded to the throne, he appointed the eunuch Lin Yanyu Commissioner of the Sweet Spring Palace, and Yanyu took considerable part in government affairs.

units.zh: 延遇病將死，言於晟曰：「臣死，惟龔澄樞可用。」
units.en: On his deathbed Yanyu told Shen, "When I am gone, only Gong Chengshu is fit to serve you."
units.literal: Yanyu, ill and near death, said to Shen: "When I die, only Gong Chengshu can be used."

units.zh: 即日擢知承宣院兼內侍省，改德陵使兼龍德宮使。
units.en: That same day Shen promoted him to head the Presentation Court while also serving in the Palace Domestic Service, then made him Commissioner of the Virtue Mausoleum and Commissioner of the Dragon Virtue Palace.
units.literal: That same day he was promoted to administer the Presentation Court while also holding the Palace Domestic Service, then transferred to Commissioner of the Virtue Mausoleum together with Commissioner of the Dragon Virtue Palace.

units.zh: 鋹嗣位，加特進、開府儀同三司、萬華宮使、驃騎大將軍，改上將軍、左龍虎軍觀軍容使、內太師，軍國之務皆決於澄樞。
units.en: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu received Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and Cavalry Grand General, then Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor. Every matter of war and state passed through his hands.
units.literal: When Chang succeeded to the throne, Chengshu was given Special Advancement, Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Commissioner of the Myriad Splendor Palace, and Cavalry Grand General; he was then changed to Grand General, Army Observer of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and Inner Grand Preceptor — all military and state affairs were decided by Chengshu.

units.zh: 澄樞與李托、薛崇譽置酷法之具，民甚苦之。
units.en: Chengshu, Li Tuo, and Xue Chongyu instituted instruments of torture, and the people endured terrible suffering.
units.literal: Chengshu, together with Li Tuo and Xue Chongyu, set up instruments of cruel law, and the people suffered greatly.

units.zh: 初，岩改名龔，有術者言不利，名龔，當敗國事，遂改名龑。
units.en: Yan had first changed his name to Gong, but a diviner warned that the name Gong would bring ruin upon the state, so he adopted the invented character instead.
units.literal: At first Yan changed his name to Gong; a diviner said it was unfavorable — the name Gong would ruin state affairs — so he changed his name to the invented character.

units.zh: 後鋹用澄樞，以其姓卒亡其國，澄樞亦被誅。
units.en: Later Chang put Chengshu in power — and the Gong surname did indeed destroy his realm. Chengshu was executed as well.
units.literal: Later Chang employed Chengshu; because of his surname he ultimately lost his state, and Chengshu was also executed.

units.zh: 李托，封州封川人。
units.en: Li Tuo came from Fengchuan in Feng Prefecture.
units.literal: Li Tuo was a native of Fengchuan in Feng Prefecture.

units.zh: 少習騎射，以謹願事龑為內府局令。
units.en: He trained in horsemanship and archery from youth and entered service under the emperor with the invented name as Director of an Inner Treasury Bureau, distinguished by his dutiful temperament.
units.literal: In youth he practiced mounted archery and, with cautious compliance, served the emperor with the invented name as Director of an Inner Treasury Bureau.

units.zh: 晟襲位，遷內侍省內侍，充宮闈諸衛押番兼秀華宮使。
units.en: When Shen took the throne, Tuo was made a Palace Attendant in the Palace Domestic Service, assigned to the palace guard rotation and Commissioner of the Splendid Beauty Palace.
units.literal: When Shen succeeded to the throne, Tuo was transferred to Palace Attendant in the Palace Domestic Service, filling the palace guard rotation duty together with Commissioner of the Splendid Beauty Palace.

units.zh: 鋹立，改玩華宮使、內侍監兼列聖、景陽二宮使。
